target_customer: Fragrance lovers, mostly millennial consumers, paying a monthly subscription for travel size designer perfumes and colognes
problem: Buying a full bottle of perfume is expensive and risky without trying it, and department store sampling is limited, so Scentbird lets people rotate samples monthly.
business_model: Consumer subscription with monthly 8 ml fragrance vials, later full size products, own brands and IP licensing

founders.name: Mariya Nurislamova
previous_startups: Deck of Scarlet (makeup palette subscription, 2016, with Scentbird team)
founders.background_notes: Listed as sole founder on the YC page and as cofounder and CEO in press.

founders.name: Rachel ten Brink
founders.background_notes: Described by Glossy as co-founder of Scentbird and Deck of Scarlet.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ecommerce, subscription billing and fulfillment of decanted fragrance vials; the hard part is supply and brand relationships, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Copyable subscription model, but brand partnerships, fulfillment scale and subscriber data give some edge; later own brands and licensing added differentiation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Beauty box players used the same model but no one absorbed the fragrance wedge; later rivals such as Scentbox appeared and Scentbird kept growing and bought Drift in 2022.

market_need_then: Fragrance is a large category where sampling is hard online. Contemporary demand evidence from 2015 was not found beyond the company's own subscription pitch and YC acceptance.

identity.logo: Monogram introduced in 2022 refresh, replacing earlier look
identity.visual_style: Clean minimalist monogram, modern fonts and textured design elements after 2022
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful and aspirational luxury, framed as a fragrance playground

branding.brand_signature: Monthly fragrance subscription of designer scents plus sister brands such as Confessions of a Rebel

rebrands.why: Modernize the brand and refocus on loyal customers, brand partners and data driven technology, per CEO

branding.community_and_virality: Influencer marketing with beauty creators for sister brand Deck of Scarlet; IP licensing collections such as Strawberry Shortcake and John Wick reported to bring in many new subscriptions.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable DTC subscription name with licensing and own brands, but evidence of community or cultural pull is limited to trade press.

outcome_analysis: Scentbird built a profitable looking consumer subscription for fragrance samples, raised only about $18.6M in a 2018 Series A and a few seed rounds, and grew to over $100M of annual revenue by 2024 per Modern Retail. It expanded into own brands, a 2022 Drift acquisition and IP licensing. It remains private and active; the main risks are rival subscriptions and reliance on brand supply.
notes: Company site returned 403 at fetch time. The 2016 seed amount comes from startupintros only and is unverified; a 2015 round of about $1M and a 2014 pre-seed appear on aggregators only and are omitted. Seed total of $5.8M over two years is reported in trade press. Series A is $18.6M per press release; aggregators report $24.6M. Series B (2019) and C (2021) exist on CB Insights with no amounts or investors, so are omitted; total raised is therefore incomplete. Revenue figures conflict: over $100M in 2024 per Modern Retail vs $36M estimate for 2023. No competitor source dated near 2015 was found, so the list is empty; Scentbox and others appear only in current comparisons. Founded year 2013 per YC page.
